questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is safe as long as no other vehicles are near you.
Can cause you to move into another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to move into another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. You may lose control and end up in another lane or off the road. Always slow down when turning.

questions.question: A motorcycle operator can be more visible by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Also use your headlight, signals, and brake light at all times.

questions.question: You should fully check your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Inspect your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.explanation: Only waiting and not drinking alcohol reduces your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your blood alcohol or make you sober.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following should you check before riding?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires.
The amount of padding on your seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: You should inspect your motorcycle:
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes only a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular and white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your ability to ride:

options.text: Starting at about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired well below the legal limit. Never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Wear reflective clothing at night to make yourself more visible. Bright colors with reflective materials help other drivers see you.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check your blind spot if you use your mirrors.
Your mirrors give you a complete view of all areas around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Assume other drivers will see your turn signal and respond correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is an important benefit of wearing a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: It is too warm to wear in hot weather.
It protects you in a crash.
You should not wear one while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket when riding. Leather protects you in a crash. Modern motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool even in warm weather.

questions.question: Before riding, which check is NOT necessary?

options.text: Test both brakes to make sure the brake light comes on.
Check that the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and all lights including the headlight, taillight, turn signals, and brake light.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that makes you and your motorcycle visible to other drivers. Bright, reflective clothing is easier for others to see.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen by other drivers?
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen by others.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other drivers and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and hazards on the road. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it has the same effect as braking. That is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, what should you be ready for?

options.text: A parked car suddenly pulling into traffic.
Other drivers seeing you and staying out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car suddenly pulling into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly pull out. It is safest to ride in the left part of your lane to create more space between your motorcycle and parked cars.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes gently, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as these have less grip.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash?

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who took a safety course.

questions.explanation: New riders who don't know how to operate their motorcycle are most likely to crash.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time. They work best together.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes and move out of their way. Speeding up will only make the tailgater drive faster too.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more it builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes it.
The easier you can avoid police.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol quickly causes it to build up in your body. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Can a motorcycle share a lane with a car?

options.text: Yes, because a motorcycle is narrow.
Yes, if there is enough space.
No, a motorcycle needs a full lane to operate safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, a motorcycle needs a full lane to operate safely.
questions.explanation: Both motorcycles and cars need the full width of a lane to operate safely. They should never share a lane.
